record.narrative: No prior claims exist, so I am registering a first wave of discovery comparisons. Because predictor labels are opaque, I focus on comparisons with clear statistical power and plausible scientific interpretability: binary predictors with adequate prevalence and continuous feature_061 as a clinically-like numeric subgroup. Main effects test whether the exposed group has a more negative dependency score (direction -1; stronger dependency) or a more positive score (direction +1; weaker dependency). Interactions test whether the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is more negative or more positive in the named subgroup than in the subgroup complement. I choose relatively common binary features to satisfy the 20-observed-cell rule, and I include age/continuous-feature subgroups to begin testing effect modification. The reported signed effects will be judged against the 10% relative clinical-significance threshold and 95% intervals, with particular attention to whether confidence limits exclude the threshold or remain too wide to support acceptance. These are associations only, not causal claims.

There is no direct evidence yet, so I am requesting the full first wave of 12 registered comparisons to obtain initial signed estimates and 95% Welch intervals. These span main effects of common binary features across several dependency scores and initial effect-modification tests using feature_034 and feature_061. Running the complete first wave is efficient because all cell sizes appear adequate from the prevalence summaries, and the results will reveal which predictor-outcome associations are near or beyond the 10% relative clinical-significance threshold versus those likely representing null or underpowered associations. In subsequent appraise/synthesize stages I will allocate follow-up to claims whose intervals suggest scientifically meaningful differences or promising interactions.

None of the valid main-effect comparisons supports a clinically significant association after considering the 10% relative threshold and 95% uncertainty. I rejected H2, H3, H6, and H8 because the signed intervals are not compatible with a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction; their point estimates are near zero and, for these outcomes, the upper credible range in the claimed direction remains below or very close to the 10% threshold. H1, H4, and H7 are unresolved but deferred: their point estimates are small, although the upper intervals just touch or slightly exceed the approximate 10% relative effect scale, so a definitive null statement is too strong given multiplicity and residual uncertainty. H5 remains active as the most promising main effect: outcome_015 with feature_021 has a positive signed estimate of 0.0168, below the approximate 0.025 threshold, but the interval extends above it. H11 is the most interesting interaction: outcome_006 has a point estimate above its much smaller relative threshold, but the interval is wide and includes zero and the opposite direction, so I request independent validation rather than accepting it. H12 is unresolved and deferred because the point estimate is in the opposite direction and the interval is too wide. H9 and H10 produced invalid interactions with zero cells in the named subgroup, most likely a value/coding issue for the binary equality condition; they remain unresolved and active, and I registered refinements using numeric equality conditions. Overall, the evidence supports associations only, not causality or generalizability, and the near-threshold results must be interpreted cautiously because multiple comparisons were performed.

Synthesis after validation: the H11 feature_002-by-feature_061 interaction on outcome_006 was the strongest first-wave candidate, but it did not replicate. The discovery estimate was +0.0161, above the approximate 10% absolute effect scale for outcome_006 (~0.0093), yet its 95% interval crossed zero and the opposite direction. The independent validation estimate was -0.0065, opposite the claimed direction, with a very wide independent interval from -0.1153 to +0.1024. Because the validation point estimate is not supportive and the intervals are inconsistent, there is no basis to accept H11. However, the validation interval remains compatible with a clinically meaningful positive effect, so I do not treat this as proof of null. I therefore close H11 as unresolved/inconclusive rather than accepting it. Scientific report so far: supported associations: none. Negative findings: H2, H3, H6, and H8 are rejected because their intervals are not compatible with a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. H9 and H10 were invalid due zero subgroup cells and are closed as unresolved measurement/coding artifacts pending refined comparisons H13 and H14. Failed or inconsistent candidates: H11 failed independent validation; H12 had a point estimate opposite its claimed direction and wide uncertainty. Unresolved but not yet validated: H1, H4, H5, H7, and H12 remain unresolved, with H5 the most promising main effect because its upper interval crosses the approximate outcome_015 10% threshold. Most informative next analyses: run H13 and H14 to repair the invalid feature_034 interaction, run H15 to test the feature_061 threshold at >=65 for outcome_006, run H16 and the new H5 parent-linked subgroup comparison to evaluate whether feature_021's effect on outcome_015 differs by feature_002, and run H17-H20 plus the new common-binary main effects to expand coverage of high-variance outcomes. All statements remain associations within this supplied dataset, not causal effects or generalizable claims.

The first wave produced no accepted claims and one promising interaction candidate failed independent validation, so I am registering a second discovery wave that is both broader and more focused. Broadly, I add untested categorical levels and binary predictors that appear to have adequate cell counts. More focused follow-up targets two near-threshold candidate exposures from the first wave: feature_037, whose outcome_012 interval just crossed the approximate 10% absolute scale, and feature_021, whose outcome_015 interval also crossed that scale. I test these candidates on outcome_014, outcome_006, and outcome_008, where the absolute outcome scale and variance make a 10% relative difference easier to detect if the association is present. I also register effect-modification comparisons using common modifiers: numeric feature_034, now using numeric equality to avoid the earlier zero-cell failure, and continuous feature_010 as a median-like high/low biomarker-like modifier. Directional hypotheses are: direction -1 claims that exposure is associated with a more negative dependency score, i.e., stronger dependency, whereas direction +1 claims that exposure is associated with a less negative dependency score, i.e., weaker dependency. For interactions, direction -1 means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast is expected to be more negative in the subgroup than in the complement; direction +1 means it is expected to be more positive. These are exploratory associations only; acceptance will require effect sizes and intervals to be compatible with a clinically meaningful 10% relative difference, with caution because of multiple comparisons.

I am requesting 12 discovery analyses chosen to balance repairing invalid interactions, following up the most promising earlier candidate, and broadening coverage of high-sensitivity dependency scores. H13 and H14 repair the feature_034 interactions that previously failed because the string equality condition produced zero cells. H16 and H25 directly follow up H5, the feature_021 association with outcome_015: H25 tests the conditional mean difference within feature_002=1, while H16 tests whether the feature_021 contrast is stronger when feature_002=1 than in its complement. H17, H19, H20, H21, and H22 test unexamined main effects of common binary predictors on outcomes with useful signal-to-threshold characteristics: outcome_014, outcome_011, outcome_008, and outcome_006. H18 adds coverage of outcome_001 for feature_034. H26 and H28 test cross-outcome associations for the two most promising first-wave exposures, feature_037 and feature_021, using outcome_014, which has a small absolute 10% threshold (~0.0093). I am deferring H15, H30-H33, and further feature_021 modifiers such as H35 to the next wave so this batch remains focused on repaired comparisons, the leading candidate, and broad high-sensitivity screening. All results remain associations in the supplied discovery data, not causal effects or generalizable conclusions.

The repaired numeric feature_034 interactions H13 and H14 now produced valid cells, but both estimates are opposite the claimed direction and their intervals include zero, null, and the clinically meaningful threshold only marginally at the positive edge. I closed them as inconclusive because they are not promising. H16 is a strong negative result for the claim that feature_021's association with outcome_015 is stronger among feature_002=1 cells: the signed interaction is -0.0332, the upper bound is far below the approximately 0.025 outcome_015 threshold, and the interval is mostly on the opposite side of zero. I rejected H16. H25, the conditional mean difference among feature_002=1 cells, is near zero and not clinically meaningful; I closed it as unresolved but not active. Together, H16 and H25 suggest that if the feature_021 association seen in H5 exists, it is not concentrated in feature_002=1 and may instead reside in the feature_002=0 complement. I registered complementary mean-difference proposals for outcome_015 and outcome_014 among feature_002=0 cells. Main-effect screening was mostly negative: H18 rejected because outcome_001 interval excludes the approximate threshold; H19 rejected because the signed effect is opposite direction and the upper bound is below the outcome_011 threshold; H17, H20, H21, and H22 are not clinically supported and are closed as inconclusive. H26 does not support outcome_014 for feature_037. The only active new candidate is H28: feature_021 on outcome_014 has a signed point estimate of +0.0157, above the approximate 10% threshold for outcome_014 (~0.0093) and in the same weaker-dependency direction as H5 on outcome_015. However, the confidence interval is wide, crosses zero, and includes values below the clinical threshold, so I am not accepting it. I request independent validation for H28 because it is the most clinically meaningful point estimate now and would test whether feature_021 shows a cross-outcome association in the discovery dataset. No claim is accepted yet; all statements remain associations and are vulnerable to multiplicity.

H28 tested feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 on outcome_014 in the claimed direction of a less negative dependency score, i.e., weaker dependency. The discovery estimate was +0.01569, above the approximate 10% absolute threshold for outcome_014 (~0.0093), but its 95% interval included zero and sub-threshold values. The independent validation estimate was +0.00979, very close to the clinical threshold and in the same direction, which is supportive in sign but not decisive. The independent interval was extremely wide, from -0.05165 to +0.07122, and the interval already accounts for the maximum number of validation comparisons in the run. Therefore, although the validation result is consistent with the discovery direction, it does not provide enough precision to support a scientifically meaningful association claim. Because this candidate arose from broad screening across many outcomes and predictors, accepting it now would be too liberal. I therefore leave H28 unresolved but defer the same comparison, because the most informative next step is not another test of the identical H28 contrast but triangulation through outcome_006 and outcome_005 and localization through the feature_002=0 complement. The earlier feature_021 pattern is now the leading unresolved signal: H5 on outcome_015 has a positive point estimate below the 0.025 threshold but an interval extending above it; H28 on outcome_014 is above threshold in discovery and borderline in validation; H16 rejected the claim that the effect is stronger in feature_002=1, and H25 was near null within feature_002=1. This suggests that if feature_021 is associated with weaker dependency, it may be concentrated in the feature_002=0 complement. Next analyses should therefore prioritize H36 and H37, the feature_002=0 complements for outcome_015 and outcome_014, and the newly registered cross-outcome tests H38 outcome_006 and H39 outcome_005 for feature_021. H29, the registered outcome_008 test of feature_021, should also remain in the next wave. No claim is accepted yet; all current positive candidates are associations within this supplied dataset, not causal effects or generalized biological conclusions.

No claim is currently due for assessment. This explore step registers refinements and new screens. The strongest unresolved signal remains feature_021 being associated with a less negative dependency score, i.e., weaker dependency, on outcome_015 and outcome_014, with validation directionally supportive but imprecise for outcome_014. The feature_002 interaction evidence suggests that, if this signal is real, it is not concentrated in feature_002=1: H16 was strongly opposite the claim that the effect is stronger among feature_002=1, and the conditional mean difference within feature_002=1 was near null. Therefore, I propose direct feature_002=0 complement tests for feature_021 on outcome_006, outcome_005, outcome_008, and outcome_012. Outcome_006 has the smallest absolute clinical threshold, so a feature_002=0-specific effect could become clinically meaningful even if the overall main effect is diluted. These comparisons are associations only; alternatives include no association, a true effect present in both feature_002 strata, or a false positive from multiple testing. I also register a common-predictor screen for feature_034 on outcome_006 in the stronger-dependency direction, because prior feature_034 main-effect estimates in direction -1 were small but positive on outcome_008 and outcome_001/outcome_014 cards, and outcome_006 has a lower absolute threshold. Finally, I register two similarly prevalent untested binary features, feature_042 on outcome_006 and feature_050 on outcome_014, with the same less-negative direction as feature_021. This is a specificity check: if feature_021 is an isolated candidate, these similar-prevalence screens should be weak or null; if they also reach threshold, the apparent feature_021 signal may reflect a broader pattern or chance screening rather than a distinctive association.

I am selecting 12 discovery analyses to test the leading unresolved feature_021 signal and evaluate whether it is specific to feature_002=0, robust across outcomes, and not merely a broad screening artifact. First, I run the registered feature_002=0 complement analyses for feature_021: H36 outcome_015, H37 outcome_014, H40 outcome_006, H41 outcome_005, H42 outcome_008, and H43 outcome_012. These test the hypothesis generated by H16 and H25: if feature_021 is associated with a less negative dependency score, the association is likely not concentrated in feature_002=1 and may be clearer in the feature_002=0 complement. Second, I run the overall cross-outcome tests H38 outcome_006, H39 outcome_005, and H29 outcome_008 to see whether the feature_021 association extends beyond the two most promising outcomes, outcome_015 and outcome_014. Third, I include specificity and alternative-predictor screens: H45 feature_042 on outcome_006, H46 feature_050 on outcome_014, and H44 feature_034 on outcome_006. If feature_021 is a distinctive candidate, these similarly prevalent binary or common binary predictors should generally remain null or weak; if they also reach clinical thresholds, the apparent feature_021 pattern may reflect broader structure, correlated biology, or chance screening rather than a focused association. All selected comparisons are associations in this discovery dataset; I will decide in appraise whether any support clinically meaningful effects and whether validation is warranted.

The new wave sharply separates a highly robust feature_021 association from weaker borderline signals. H38 and H40 accept cleanly for the claimed positive, less-negative dependency direction: on outcome_006, feature_021=1 versus 0 has discovery estimates of +0.8019 overall and +0.7897 within feature_002=0, with 95% intervals entirely above the approximate 10% absolute clinical threshold (~0.0093) and with adequate cell counts. The magnitude is large and not near the null; although these claims are correlated and arose from the same discovery sample, even conservative multiplicity reasoning supports accepting them as scientifically meaningful associations in this dataset. They support the interpretation that feature_021 is associated with weaker dependency for the outcome_006 dependency score, not that feature_021 causes weaker dependency or that the association generalizes. H40 additionally supports localization to feature_002=0, while H38 shows that the association is not confined only to the subgroup-selected contrast.

The feature_002=0 complement effects on outcome_015 and outcome_005 are more ambiguous and are worth preserving. H36 estimates +0.0335 and H41 estimates +0.0305; both point estimates exceed the approximate 0.025 clinical threshold, and both have 95% intervals excluding zero, but both lower bounds are far below the clinical threshold. Thus the uncertainty is compatible with subthreshold positive effects. Given the number of registered comparisons and the post-hoc localization to feature_002=0, I do not accept these moderate effects solely on discovery evidence. I request independent validation for H36 as the representative localized feature_002=0/outcome_015 signal; if it validates, H41 becomes more credible as cross-outcome triangulation.

H43 is rejected because the claimed positive effect on outcome_012 is opposite to the observed effect and the upper bound, +0.0144, is below the approximate 0.0248 threshold. H37, H29, H39, and H42 do not support accepted positive clinical effects: their estimates are small, opposite, or below threshold, although their intervals remain wide enough to prevent firm rejection. I close them as unresolved low-priority. H37 is especially inconsistent with a simple broader feature_021/outcome_014 localization because it is negative within feature_002=0; together with H28, it suggests the outcome_014 result is weak and unstable, so I close H28 as unresolved. H44, H45, and H46 serve as specificity screens and do not show positive clinically meaningful effects for feature_034, feature_042, or feature_050, but their intervals are not sufficiently informative to reject all possible effects. Overall, the strongest evidence now is for feature_021 on outcome_006, with a secondary unresolved localized signal on outcome_015 and outcome_005.

The new validation evidence weakens the secondary feature_021 pattern but does not undermine the accepted outcome_006 result. H36 tested feature_021=1 versus feature_021=0 on outcome_015 within feature_002=0, in the claimed weaker-dependency direction. Its discovery estimate was positive and clinically suggestive in sign (+0.0335, 95% interval roughly [0.0062, 0.0607]) but imprecise at the lower end. Independent validation was essentially null in that direction (+0.00041) and very wide (about [-0.0428, 0.0436]), and the independent interval already includes multiplicity accounting. I therefore do not accept H36. I also do not formally reject a clinically meaningful effect because the independent interval still includes values above the approximate outcome_015 threshold; the correct conclusion is that the localized feature_021/outcome_015 claim is unsupported and low priority. This in turn weakens the analogous discovery-only claim H41 on outcome_005 within feature_002=0, so I leave H41 unresolved and deferred rather than requesting another validation of that localized pattern now. The accepted findings remain H38 and H40: feature_021 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 dependency score overall and within feature_002=0, with large and precise discovery intervals well above the approximate 10% absolute threshold for outcome_006. These are dataset associations, not causal or generalizable claims. H26 tested feature_037 on outcome_014 in the stronger-dependency direction. The discovery estimate was opposite the claim, while the independent validation estimate was small but in the claimed direction (+0.0086), just below the approximate outcome_014 threshold and with an interval spanning zero, subthreshold, threshold, and opposite effects. Combined evidence is too weak and inconsistent to accept or to make a negative inference. H11 tested an outcome_006 feature_002-by-feature_061 interaction; the discovery point was positive and threshold-crossing but very wide, and the independent validation estimate was opposite direction with an extremely wide interval. Validation does not support the interaction; the interval remains too imprecise to reject any possible interaction, so I leave H11 unresolved but close it as a low-priority screen. The next most informative analyses are direct stratum characterization of the accepted outcome_006 feature_021 association, especially feature_002=1, and broader feature_021 screens on outcomes not yet tested. If feature_021 truly has an outcome-specific effect, the cross-outcome tests should be mostly weak or null; if several reach clinically meaningful thresholds, the effect may be broader. I defer several older low-priority interaction and main-effect screens to prioritize feature_021 strata, feature_037 on outcome_006, and categorical feature screens.

No evidence assessments are due, so the main action is to refocus the next discovery wave on the one robust result so far: feature_021=1 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 dependency score in this dataset (H38 and H40 accepted). The key scientific questions are now: (1) Is this association reproducible across important strata of accepted effect size, not merely in feature_002=0; (2) does it differ by prevalent binary features or age; (3) is it outcome-specific for outcome_006 or part of a broader dependency pattern; and (4) is it distinct from other similarly prevalent predictors. I therefore propose direct conditional mean-difference tests for feature_021 on outcome_006 within feature_034=1 and within feature_060=1, both expected positive if the accepted association is broad and robust. I also propose two interaction tests: feature_021-by-feature_034 and feature_021-by-feature_061>=55, using a positive interaction direction to test whether the less-negative association is stronger in the subgroup than in the complement; the anticipated direction is uncertain because no prior evidence strongly predicts modification. For outcome specificity, I propose a single additional overall feature_021 test on outcome_003, a low absolute threshold outcome not yet screened, rather than testing every remaining outcome; this balances breadth against multiplicity. For predictor specificity on the accepted outcome, I propose two similar-prevalence binary markers, feature_027 and feature_050, in the same less-negative direction; a null result would make feature_021 more distinctive, while a threshold-positive result would suggest a broader marker axis or correlated structure. Finally, I add a categorical screen on outcome_006 comparing feature_055 level_001 with level_003 to maintain predictor diversity. I defer several broad outcome_014/feature_005 and feature_021 outcome-panel claims that have no evidence or low prior yield, and also defer H48 because the localized feature_002=0/outcome_005 pattern was not supported by validation; this keeps the active set focused on stratum characterization, specificity, and a small number of categorical/broad screens. All proposed claims remain associations within this dataset, not causal effects or claims of generalizability. Alternative explanations include no association, opposite-direction effects, subgroup-specific heterogeneity, confounding by correlated predictors, or false-positive discovery due to multiple testing.

I am selecting 12 registered, previously untested discovery analyses. The goal is to characterize the robust outcome_006/feature_021 association rather than continue broad, low-priority screening. First, I test stratum reproducibility and modification of feature_021 on outcome_006: H47 within feature_002=1, H55 within feature_034=1, and H56 within feature_060=1; plus interaction analyses H57 versus feature_034=1 and H58 versus feature_061>=55. These distinguish a broad association from one localized by feature_002 or other prevalent predictors, and assess whether subgroup differences are clinically meaningful. Second, I test outcome specificity with H59 on outcome_003 to determine whether feature_021 marks a broader dependency phenotype or is outcome-specific. Third, I test predictor specificity for the accepted outcome_006 signal using H60 feature_027, H61 feature_050, and H62 feature_055 level_001 versus level_003; threshold-positive alternative predictors would reduce confidence that feature_021 is distinctive. Finally, I include H27 feature_037, H31 feature_054, and H33 feature_063 on outcome_006 as diverse predictor screens. No validation is requested now; all estimates will be assessed in appraise against clinical thresholds, interval precision, cell adequacy, and multiplicity.

The new stratum analyses confirm that the accepted outcome_006 feature_021 association is broad across major binary strata in this supplied dataset. H47 within feature_002=1, H55 within feature_034=1, and H56 within feature_060=1 have very large signed estimates in the weaker-dependency direction: +0.8144, +0.7976, and +0.7999, respectively, with 95% intervals far above the approximate clinical threshold for outcome_006 (~0.0093) and with adequate cell counts. I therefore accept these as dataset associations, consistent with H38 and H40, and close them because the central feature_021/outcome_006 pattern has been characterized across the key strata. They remain associations within this dataset only, not causal effects or generalizable claims; the strata are overlapping and correlated, so these are not independent replications, but their magnitude makes multiplicity and chance unlikely explanations for the main pattern. H57 and H58 test whether the association is stronger in the feature_034=1 or age>=55 subgroups. Both have negative signed interaction point estimates and intervals that include zero, threshold-crossing positive values, and threshold-crossing opposite-direction values; there is no clinically meaningful evidence of stronger effect modification, so I leave them unresolved as low-priority and close them. The age interaction also depends on a predictor with substantial missingness, so it could reflect selection under missingness as well as real heterogeneity. H59 tests feature_021 on outcome_003. The signed estimate is tiny (+0.0015) and its upper bound (+0.0212) is below the approximate outcome_003 threshold (~0.025), so the evidence does not support a clinically meaningful positive feature_021 association for outcome_003; I reject that specific positive clinical claim. Alternative outcome_006 predictor screens were generally uninformative or borderline: feature_027 is below threshold with wide uncertainty, feature_055 level comparison is opposite to the claimed direction, feature_037 is borderline but imprecise, feature_054 is weak, and feature_063 is opposite to the claimed direction. The one specificity screen worth further checking is H61, feature_050 on outcome_006, because it has prevalence similar to feature_021, a point estimate well above threshold (+0.0262), and a wide interval that includes both clinically meaningful positive and opposite effects. I request independent validation for H61 because it is the most informative non-central borderline association: if it validates, feature_050 may represent a related predictor axis or potential confounder; if it is null, it strengthens the distinctiveness of feature_021 for outcome_006 in this dataset. No other validation request is made because the accepted feature_021 pattern is already unusually large and internally consistent across strata.

The newly released validation evidence resolves two weak claims without adding new accepted findings. For H28, feature_021=1 versus 0 on outcome_014 in the claimed less-negative direction, discovery was +0.0157 with 95% interval [-0.0247, 0.0561], and independent validation was +0.0098 with a wide multiplicity-adjusted interval [-0.0516, 0.0712]. Both estimates have the same sign and are near the approximate outcome_014 clinical threshold (~0.0093), but the independent interval includes zero and spans both subthreshold and large threshold-crossing values. This is not sufficient to accept a clinically meaningful association, and it is not sufficient to reject one because clinically meaningful positive values remain compatible with the data. I therefore leave H28 unresolved but close it as a low-priority secondary claim. For H61, feature_050=1 versus 0 on outcome_006 in the less-negative direction, discovery was +0.0262 with 95% interval [-0.0146, 0.0671], while independent validation was nearly null at +0.0026 with multiplicity-adjusted interval [-0.0580, 0.0631]. The validation does not support feature_050 as a robust alternative predictor for outcome_006 in this supplied dataset. The independent interval nevertheless remains too wide to rule out a threshold effect, so H61 should be closed as unresolved rather than rejected. This strengthens the interpretation that feature_050 is not a major competing marker on outcome_006, although it does not prove feature_050 has exactly zero effect. The central accepted evidence remains that feature_021=1 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 dependency score: H38 overall, H40 within feature_002=0, H47 within feature_002=1, H55 within feature_034=1, and H56 within feature_060=1, all with estimates near +0.80 and intervals far above the outcome_006 threshold. These are dataset associations, not causal effects or generalizable claims. The validation results suggest that the most informative next analysis is outcome specificity for feature_021: test the remaining outcome_012, outcome_002, outcome_011, and outcome_001 panels, and activate the already registered outcome_016, outcome_009, outcome_010, outcome_013, outcome_007, and outcome_004 panels. If most of these are weak or null, the feature_021 finding is outcome_006-specific in this dataset; if several intervals clear the respective clinical thresholds, feature_021 may mark a broader less-negative dependency phenotype. I do not request further validation now because no new strong borderline non-central main effect warrants it: feature_050 validation is weak, feature_037 evidence is inconsistent, and feature_021 interactions have been imprecise or opposite in sign.

No evidence assessments are due, so this stage should register the next focused set of comparisons. The only robust dataset finding so far is that feature_021=1 is associated with a much less negative outcome_006 dependency score: H38 overall and accepted strata within feature_002=0/1, feature_034=1, and feature_060=1 all have large positive signed contrasts far above the approximate outcome_006 threshold (~0.0093). The most informative follow-up is therefore to test whether that association survives important demographic and marker-based contexts, and whether similarly prevalent alternative markers can reproduce it on outcome_006. I propose simple effect mean differences for feature_021 within older age, feature_061>=55, and younger age, feature_061<55, both claimed in the less-negative direction. These are not independent replications because the age interaction H58 was already weak and imprecise, but they directly test whether the association is confined to one age stratum or persists across observed age. They also expose a plausible alternative: age missingness or selection in observed age could make these subgroup effects misleading. I propose joint strata where feature_034 and feature_060 are both 1 and both 0. If the feature_021/outcome_006 association remains large and threshold-clearing in both joint strata, it is not merely driven by the marginal overlap of these prevalent binary features; if one joint stratum weakens, this would suggest context-dependence or correlated marker structure. For predictor specificity on the accepted outcome, I propose four similarly prevalent binary screens, feature_012, feature_065, feature_052, and feature_020, all in the less-negative outcome_006 direction. These have prevalence near feature_021 and sufficient cell sizes, so a threshold-positive association would indicate a broader marker axis or potential confounding, whereas null or imprecise subthreshold results would make feature_021 more distinctive for outcome_006 in this supplied dataset. I also keep four untested outcome-specificity claims active, H63 outcome_012, H64 outcome_002, H65 outcome_011, and H66 outcome_001, to balance the focused follow-up with the broader goal of determining whether feature_021 marks a narrower or broader dependency phenotype. I defer the remaining feature_021 outcome-panel claims H49-H54 for now because the accepted central pattern and predictor-specificity questions are more directly informative. All proposed claims remain associations within this dataset only, not causal claims or claims of generalizability.

I select the twelve currently active, previously untested claims to resolve the two most informative open questions: outcome specificity for feature_021 and robustness/predictor specificity for the central outcome_006/feature_021 association. H63-H66 test feature_021 overall on outcome_012, outcome_002, outcome_011, and outcome_001, respectively. These complement H38/H40/H47/H55/H56 and existing secondary outcome tests; if their signed lower bounds clear the outcome-specific 10% clinical thresholds, feature_021 may mark a broader dependency phenotype. If they are weak, opposite, or imprecise, the feature_021 finding remains more specific to outcome_006 in this supplied dataset. H67-H70 test outcome_006 feature_021 simple effects by observed age strata and by joint feature_034/feature_060 status. These are not independent replications but assess whether the very large less-negative association is confined to particular demographic or marker contexts, and whether joint strata reveal correlated marker structure or small-cell instability. H71-H74 test four similarly prevalent binary predictors on outcome_006 in the same less-negative direction. If any clears the outcome_006 threshold, this suggests a related predictor axis, correlated marker structure, or potential confounding of the feature_021 specificity interpretation; if they remain null or imprecise, feature_021 becomes more distinctive for outcome_006 in this dataset. No validation is requested at this stage because the selected analyses are new discovery estimates and no currently available evidence indicates that a single borderline non-central claim is decisive for the central interpretation.

I assessed the twelve new discovery estimates against outcome-specific 10% absolute thresholds. For outcome_006, the threshold is approximately 0.0093; for outcome_012, outcome_002, outcome_011, and outcome_001 it is approximately 0.0248, 0.0260, 0.0301, and 0.0415, respectively. The feature_021 association remains the dominant feature_021/outcome_006 finding: it is also large in observed age strata and in joint feature_034/feature_060 double-positive and double-negative strata, so I accepted H67-H70 and closed them. These age-stratum results exclude missing feature_061 observations, so they support persistence only within observed-age contexts and are not generalizable claims. Outcome specificity for feature_021 is increasingly narrow: H63 (outcome_012) and H64 (outcome_002) have intervals below the positive clinical threshold and point estimates slightly opposite, so the positive less-negative claims are rejected; H66 (outcome_001) has an upper bound just below threshold, also supporting rejection of a clinically meaningful positive association. H65 (outcome_011) is borderline threshold-compatible but weak and not robust, so it remains unresolved but closed. The predictor screens on outcome_006 were mixed: feature_012 and feature_065 are non-prioritized and remain unresolved because their intervals cross the threshold; feature_052 shows a strong opposite point estimate, so the claimed positive less-negative association is rejected, though a new reversed unresolved claim is registered because a potentially meaningful more-negative association remains possible. The most informative new result is H74: feature_020=1 is associated with a much less-negative outcome_006 score, signed estimate +0.0595 with lower bound +0.0148, above the approximate 0.0093 threshold. This could represent an additional predictor axis, a correlated marker structure, or a partial confounding source for the feature_021/outcome_006 pattern. I therefore request independent validation for H74 rather than for H73, because H74 is the only new positive threshold-clearing association and is more directly relevant to interpreting the specificity of the central feature_021 finding.

The newly released validation and response-deadline evidence materially changes the interpretation of feature_020 on outcome_006, while leaving the central feature_021/outcome_006 association unchanged.
